newsitem.title: USA: Cytyc, Mead Johnson to co-promote pap test.
newsitem.headline: Cytyc, Mead Johnson to co-promote pap test.

text.p: Cytyc Corp has entered an agreement with Mead Johnson & Co, a division of Bristol-Myers Squibb Co, under which the companies will co-promote Cytyc's ThinPrep Pap Test for cervical cancer screening, Cytyc said.

As part of the multiyear agreement, announced Wednesday, Mead Johnson will use its sales force to help promote the test to about 15,000 obstetricians and gynecologists throughout the United States, Cytyc said.
Cytyc shares were up 3-1/4 to 22-7/8 early Thursday afternoon.
The ThinPrep Pap Test was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in May 1996 as a replacement for the conventional Pap smear preparation, Cytyc said.

The company said clinical trials have shown the ThinPrep Pap Test to be significantly more effective than the conventional smear for the detection of low-grade and more severe lesions in a variety of patient populations and to significantly improve specimen quality.
Cytyc launched the ThinPrep Pap Test in January 1997 and has promoted the test through its own 55-person sales force.
